title: GitHub native stacked PRs: each PR targets the branch below

pins.note: Stack model: bottom PR targets main, each layer targets the branch below
Each PR shows only its layer's diff
Key rule: dependencies must live in the same or a lower layer

insight: Stacks are now a host-native concept (GA 2026-10-06) driven by the gh stack CLI, with server-side cascading rebase when a lower layer merges.
gitgud: Claude's pick: show stacks as a unit in the graph and restack descendants locally after an amend; leave PR creation to the browser.

title: Graphite CLI quick start: stacking workflow

pins.note: Two goals: simplify sharp git edges (rebasing) and enable stacking
AI Reviews and Agents sections: review is the product now
GT MCP listed: Graphite exposes stacking to agents
Workflow: create, stack, address feedback, sync from trunk

insight: The incumbent stacking tool wraps rebasing behind create/modify/restack/sync verbs and now sits inside Cursor (acquired Dec 2025).
gitgud: Claude's pick: steal the verb set (modify = amend + restack above) as GUI actions; don't depend on Graphite's service.

title: GitButler for coding agents: but agent setup

pins.note: One command installs a skill + VCS policy for the agent
Agents commit selected hunks by ID; rest stays uncommitted
Vendor benchmark: ~80% fewer commands vs plain Git
but oplog restores earlier state before publishing

insight: GitButler steers agents through a skill file and a CLI with hunk IDs, history-edit commands and an op log; the human reviews the same branches in the desktop app.
gitgud: Claude's pick: steal hunk IDs, op log and a setup command; avoid requiring a virtual-branch workspace.

title: Parallel agents in one workspace vs worktrees

pins.note: Branch routing is the agent's job; prompt stays small
Agents must call out overlap when touching the same file
Comparison table: one shared dir vs one dir per agent
Setup cost: reuse one install and dev server

insight: GitButler's answer to worktree setup cost is several active branches in one working directory, at the price of shared runtime state.
gitgud: Claude's pick: support both, but gitgud's proposals need neither: agents propose commits from the one working copy without moving branches.

title: Codex review pane: review scopes and inline findings

pins.note: Review pane: line feedback, then stage, revert, commit or push
Scopes: Unstaged, Staged, Commit, Branch, Last turn
Shows all repo changes, not only what Codex edited
Review findings rendered as inline comments in the diff

insight: OpenAI built a mini Git GUI inside the agent app: diff scopes including 'last turn', chunk staging and revert, commit/push/PR.
gitgud: Claude's pick: a 'by agent turn / by proposal' diff scope is worth stealing; gitgud should be the place this review happens, not each agent app.

title: Official MCP git server: tool list

pins.note: Tools mirror plain git verbs: status, diffs, commit, add...
git_commit commits directly: no review gate
git_add takes file paths only, no hunks

insight: The reference server is a thin, hardened CLI mirror: it disables hooks, signing and repo-defined drivers, and offers no proposal/approval concept.
gitgud: Claude's pick: gitgud's MCP should expose hunk-level 'propose', not 'commit'; real commits (with hooks and signing) happen when Max approves.

title: git history reword / split

pins.note: Why: rebase -i can leave you in a conflicted state
reword: no worktree/index touch, updates descendant branches
split: pick hunks like add -p into a new parent commit
Refuses merge commits and any conflicting operation

insight: Git now ships targeted, refuse-on-conflict history edits (reword/split 2.54, fixup 2.55, drop 2.56) built on git replay.
gitgud: Claude's pick: map these to direct-manipulation actions with a preview, falling back to own replay logic where git history is still experimental.

title: Agents start >40% of PRs; commits 34.3B

pins.note: More than 40% of PRs start with an agent (17% in March)
Repos with agent config file: 8x commits
Merged PRs 1.3B in the 12 months to Sept 2026

insight: Commit volume nearly tripled in a year and review is now how developers shape agent output.
gitgud: Claude's pick: optimise gitgud for reviewing many agent-made changes fast, not for authoring.

title: Claude Code: parallel sessions with worktrees

pins.note: --worktree flag, .worktreeinclude, cleanup, non-git hooks
Each session gets its own checkout and branch
Enforced isolation: edits to main checkout blocked
Copy gitignored files into worktrees

insight: Claude Code defaults parallel work to worktrees under .claude/worktrees with branch worktree-<name>, and skips repo-local filter drivers (LFS pointers result).
gitgud: Claude's pick: list these worktrees in gitgud's sidebar and offer an LFS 'hydrate' and 'turn into proposal' action.

title: git absorb: automatic fixup targets

pins.note: 5.8k stars: real demand for automatic fixups
Port of hg absorb: fold fixes into the right ancestor
One command: absorb --and-rebase
Or inspect fixup! commits, then autosquash

insight: Absorb finds the target commit per staged hunk by commutation, removing the 'find the SHA, rebase -i' chore.
gitgud: Claude's pick: an 'Absorb' button that previews hunk → commit assignments before applying.

title: AI in the development workflow: committing and reviewing

pins.note: Committing and reviewing code: only 10.2% mostly AI
Search for answers: 54.1% mostly AI
Most resistance for high-responsibility tasks

insight: Developers hand search and docs to AI but keep committing and reviewing for themselves (58.7% don't plan to use AI there).
gitgud: Claude's pick: AI drafts, human decides: proposals and opt-in messages, never silent commits.
